what: Cloud prices read for the compute estimate in solver/PLAN.md §6a and docs/_reports/2026-10-01-plan-revision.md. Prices are as fetched on the date below; they move, and none of them is a quote. USD, per hour, on-demand, before tax.
fetched_by: SOLVER, curl/Node fetch from this machine; read only, no account, no spend

gpu.read_from: the page's own structured data (schema.org Offer per GPU)
https://console.vast.ai/api/v0/bundles/ (the public offer search behind the pricing page); filter: 1 GPU, rentable, verified, on-demand; field dph_total
the on-demand 1x GPU table on the page
gpu.note: Lambda lists no RTX 4090. Prices are plus applicable sales tax/VAT.

cpu.read_from: https://www.hetzner.com/_resources/app/data/app/live_data_prices.json (the page's live price data); product keys read from the page
https://b0.p.awsstatic.com/pricing/2.0/meteredUnitMaps/ec2/USD/current/ec2-ondemand-without-sec-sel/US%20East%20(N.%20Virginia)/Linux/index.json (the data behind the on-demand pricing page)
cpu.note: c7a has no simultaneous multithreading, so one vCPU is one physical core (AWS c7a documentation; not re-read here — confirm before relying on it). Spot prices are lower and were not read.

cpu.provider: Vast.ai (a GPU host with many cores)
cpu.read_from: https://console.vast.ai/api/v0/bundles/ filter cpu_cores_effective >= 64, rentable, verified, on-demand
cpu.note: Single marketplace listings: availability and reliability are not guaranteed, and a listing can disappear. A 'core' here is a hardware thread as the host reports it.
